source.title: A neural computational model of incentive salience.

confidence_rationale: An explicit computational model whose functional form is near-identical to MECH-436: a cached, previously-learned incentive value modulated multiplicatively on-the-fly by a physiological-state gain factor (kappa-like), so that cue-triggered 'wanting' rises with the relevant appetite even without re-learning. Mapping fidelity is unusually high for an architectural/mechanism claim, which is weighted heavily; source is a foundational, well-cited model paper, knocked slightly because it is a model validated against existing electrophysiology rather than a fresh empirical test, and the transfer from rat mesolimbic Pavlovian cues to REE's coarse per-axis drive vector carries moderate risk.
failure_signatures: The state-modulation is multiplicative on a cached learned value, not additive: if REE's per-object incentive token has near-zero learned base_value the drive term cannot move the argmax (matches the V3-EXQ-514q in-run finding that a tiny per-axis drive spread cannot flip an object-score-dominated most_wanted).

Dynamic enhancement in the model is cue-SPECIFIC (raises salience of the appropriate CS without changing others); a REE implementation that applies a single scalar drive gain across all candidate objects would not reproduce the modelled selectivity.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Cue-triggered incentive salience ('wanting') cannot be captured by cached predictive value (temporal-difference) alone; it is recomputed at cue re-encounter by integrating prior learning with the current physiological state, so a model must modulate previously-learned values by appetite/addiction states to reproduce real-time fluctuations in wanting.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-436's incentive-salience amplitude ~ base_value*(1+kappa*per_axis_drive) is exactly this construction: the SD-057 per-object incentive token supplies the cached base_value, and the homeostatic per-axis drive supplies the state factor that scales it at recall, so the most-wanted object tracks the currently-most-depleted axis dissociably from the liking/consummatory target.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The model's state factor acts on a learned cached value of a Pavlovian cue in rat mesolimbic circuitry; REE's per-axis homeostatic drive is a coarser engineered scalar and its 'objects' are foraging resources, not conditioned cues. The model demonstrates the FORM is sufficient to produce drive-modulated wanting in principle, but says nothing about whether the V3 P2 foraging env delivers an argmax-relevant drive spread -- precisely the substrate-ceiling gap MECH-436 carries.
mapping.source_context: Computational model fit to rat behavioural and ventral-pallidum/mesolimbic electrophysiology across natural salt appetite and drug-induced sensitization states.

confidence_components.notes: Mapping_fidelity weighted heavily because the claim is a mechanism/form claim and the paper supplies almost exactly that form. Transfer_risk moderate: rat appetite axis -> REE per-axis drive vector.
